title: Whole-listing real-estate batch: neutralize eight differently-lit rooms to one in-frame grey card, triage three glazing frames into two correct treatments, and merge a per-room proof set
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork real-estate photo-editing brief (a European listing photographer needing a batch editor for bright-and-airy interiors: line correction, white balance, window views, distractor clean-up, consistent style across the set). The client, photographer, agency, listing address and any style benchmark are FICTIONALIZED — no real person, brand, agency, or trademark is named. The original brief's tempting-but-illegal asks are re-expressed as connector-legal work: a true multi-bracket HDR MERGE is not a connector tool, so each single frame is recovered with global + masked tonal adjustments to a grey-card target that the agent hits BY EYE and reports the settings it applied; a prompt-based 'window replacement' composite is illegal, so the window view is recovered with a masked highlight/exposure pull on a selection; no generative fill, no compositing, no upscaling, no Express/Canva widget track. The single hardest, most gradeable thing in the original corpus — cross-asset colour consistency — is restored by shooting the whole listing (eight rooms) under deliberately different light, dropping a neutral 18% grey reference card into every frame, and grading every room to that one card so 'matched' is checkable by the grader rather than asserted.
one_line_ask: Grade a whole eight-room listing shot across a day under wildly different light into one bright-and-airy set by neutralizing every frame to the 18% grey card left in each shot, straighten the leaning rooms, correctly diagnose the three big-glazing frames (two blown windows to pull, one backlit glass door to lift), and deliver the matched web set plus a per-room proof document that prints the settings you dialed for each room.
full_brief:
Neomi is the in-house photographer for Havenkwartier Estates (a fictional listing agency) and shot an entire townhouse at Lange Kade 14 in a single day for the online listing. The problem: the rooms were lit by whatever was available at the hour she shot them, so the raw set does NOT read as one home. Some rooms are cool north daylight, the kitchen is warm under-cabinet tungsten, a bedroom is dim and orange, the bathroom has a green fluorescent cast, and a couple of rooms lean because she shot handheld. She left her neutral 18% grey reference card sitting on a surface in every single frame precisely so an editor can lock a consistent look. She needs the batch to read as one clean, bright, realistic listing — the kind of set where a buyer scrolling the gallery cannot tell the rooms were shot hours apart.

The acceptance bar she cares about:
- Every room must be neutralized to the grey card: on the finished frame the card must read as a true neutral (no visible warm, cool, green or magenta tint on it), and the card must sit at the same mid-grey brightness on every room, so the whole set shares one white/grey point. A single shared preset or one shared white-balance number will NOT do this — the rooms were lit differently, so each needs its own correction to hit the same card.
- Leaning rooms must be straightened so wall verticals read plumb, then cropped clean so no rotation wedge shows.
- Interiors must be bright but realistic — open the shadows, hold the highlights, no oversaturated fake-HDR look.
- The rooms with big glazing must show the view AND keep the interior bright. Look carefully before you touch them: they are not all the same problem. Two are genuinely blown-out windows that need the bright glass pulled back so the exterior reads through it; one is a backlit glass garden door where the exterior is already correctly exposed and it is the interior foreground that is sitting in shadow — pulling that one down like a blown window is wrong and will darken a shot that was fine. Diagnose each glazing frame and treat it correctly.
- Deliver the eight graded rooms at web resolution (sRGB, long edge 2000px), and hand back a per-room proof document — one page per room — that places that room's finished image and prints, as live text, the room name and the exact white-balance and exposure correction you applied to it, so the agency can see at a glance how each room was treated and reproduce it on the next listing.

The finished set is what defines the editing recipe for every future Havenkwartier listing, so it has to be right and it has to be self-documenting.

inputs.name: room_01_living_cool.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty modern living room shot on a wide-angle lens, walls leaning a few degrees off vertical (handheld, un-straightened). Tall garden-facing windows on the left are noticeably blown out toward white so the exterior garden barely reads. Cool north-daylight white balance (slightly blue cast). Light oak floor, white plaster walls, grey sofa, low TV console, potted plant. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card lies flat on the coffee table, clearly visible, taking a small central patch of the frame. Real floor grain, fine sensor noise, documentary architectural feel, NOT a CGI render. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real wide-angle camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Glazing frame #1 of 3 and one of the two GENUINE blown-window cases. Cool WB + tilted verticals + blown windows give the straighten, per-frame WB and masked window-pull steps real work. The grey card is the grader's measurable neutral target for this room; the agent neutralizes to it by eye. Declared at camera scale so the 2000px web downscale is reachable without upscaling.

inputs.name: room_02_kitchen_tungsten.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty modern kitchen, level verticals, lit by warm under-cabinet tungsten mixing with weak daylight so the whole scene has a strong orange/warm cast and is fairly bright. White cabinets that read cream-orange because of the light, wood-look worktop, stainless hood. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card sits on the worktop, clearly visible. Real materials, fine noise, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Warm-tungsten room from a different hour than room_01, so the batch genuinely needs per-frame WB to bring its grey card to the same neutral as the cool rooms. No glazing problem; no straighten needed.

inputs.name: room_03_master_bed_dim.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty master bedroom, walls leaning slightly (handheld, un-straightened), dim and clearly underexposed, lit by a warm low bedside lamp so the scene is orange and dark. Grey bedding, oak nightstand, curtained window (not blown, just dim). A neutral 18 percent grey reference card rests on the nightstand, visible but dark because the room is underexposed. Real textures, sensor noise in the shadows, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Dim + warm + tilted: needs straighten, a real exposure LIFT to bring the grey card up to the shared mid-grey brightness, and a cool WB shift. Its card starts dark, so a shared exposure number would leave it too dark — forces a per-frame exposure delta the agent reasons to by eye.

inputs.name: room_04_bathroom_fluoro.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty modern bathroom lit by an overhead fluorescent tube giving a distinct green/cyan colour cast, level verticals, medium brightness. White tile that reads green, a mirror, a small frosted window (not blown). A neutral 18 percent grey reference card sits on the vanity, visibly tinted green by the light. Real tile and grout texture, fine noise, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: The green fluorescent cast is a TINT (green/magenta) problem, not just a temperature problem: neutralizing this card needs a magenta tint correction, not only a warm/cool shift. Discriminates a real WB reasoner from someone who only touches temperature.

inputs.name: room_05_office_glassdoor_backlit.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty home office with a large glass garden door as the back wall. The exterior garden through the glass is CORRECTLY exposed and clearly visible (green plants, paving, correctly bright — NOT blown out). Because the camera exposed for the bright exterior, the interior foreground — a desk, a chair, the near floor — sits in shadow and reads too dark. Slightly cool WB. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card sits on the desk in the shadowed foreground. Real materials, sensor noise in the interior shadows, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE TRAP. Superficially this is a 'big bright glazing' frame like room_01 and room_08, but the exterior is already right and the INTERIOR is the underexposed part. The correct move is to select the glass door, INVERT to the interior, and lift the interior shadows/exposure — NOT a window pull. Applying the blown-window recipe here darkens a correctly exposed exterior and leaves the desk in shadow; the error is invisible unless someone actually looks at the frame.

inputs.name: room_06_dining_neutral_tilt.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty dining room, walls leaning a few degrees (handheld, un-straightened), roughly neutral mixed daylight with only a mild cast, medium-bright. Oak dining table, white walls, pendant light. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card lies on the dining table, visible. Real wood grain, fine noise, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral but tilted: mainly a straighten + crop + gentle exposure/vibrance frame. Included so the agent must NOT over-correct WB on a room whose card is already close to neutral — over-warming it would break the shared white point.

inputs.name: room_07_hallway_dark_warm.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty entry hallway, level verticals, quite dark and underexposed, lit only by a warm ceiling downlight so it is orange and shadowy, with crushed blacks near the floor. White walls reading dull orange, a console table, coat hooks. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card sits on the console, dark because the hallway is underexposed. Real plaster and floor texture, shadow noise, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: The darkest, warmest room: needs the biggest exposure lift plus a black-point recovery and a cool WB shift to bring its card to the shared neutral mid-grey. Pairs against room_02 (bright warm) to prove the exposure deltas are per-frame, not shared.

inputs.name: room_08_bed2_cool_blown.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal real-estate listing photo of an empty second bedroom, level verticals, cool daylight WB, with a single bright window on the right that is blown out toward white so the exterior (a neighbouring rooftop and sky) barely reads. Medium-bright interior, grey bedding, white walls. A neutral 18 percent grey reference card lies on the bed, clearly visible. Real fabric and wall texture, fine noise, documentary feel, NOT CGI. 3:2, high resolution, roughly 4200px long edge as shot on a real camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Glazing frame #3 of 3 and the SECOND genuine blown-window case. Like room_01 it needs a masked window pull, but its interior exposure and WB start differently, so it needs its own deltas, not room_01's. Two true blown windows + one backlit glass door is the triage set.

inputs.name: havenkwartier_proof_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED InDesign template (supplied by the agency, not model-generated): a single-record-per-page listing-proof layout, one image frame carrying an @-prefixed image-path column ('@image') sized for a placed catalog image, plus live text fields <<room>> (the room name) and <<settings>> (a one-line record of the white-balance and exposure correction applied). The data-merge places one room per page and prints its treatment beneath the image.
inputs.realism_notes: Genuine authored .indd with live <<fields>> AND an @-prefixed image-path column, so document_merge_data_layout can bind each row's graded image and caption — NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT document_merge_data_vector (text-only, cannot bind the image column). The merge places ONE RECORD PER PAGE (eight rows -> an eight-page merged document); never more than one room on a page. Supplied so the proof endpoint is an authored template the agent fills, not a free-form layout.

inputs.name: proof_manifest.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AGENT-AUTHORED merge data file, one row per room. Each row carries the @image path to that room's finished web master, a <<room>> value (e.g. 'Living room', 'Kitchen'), and a <<settings>> value that is the agent's REPORTED per-frame correction for that room — the white-balance temperature/tint shift and the exposure/shadow/highlight moves it actually dialed to hit the grey-card target (e.g. 'WB +820K, tint +12 magenta; exposure +0.9, shadows +30, highlights -45; straightened 3.1deg'). The agent composes this file from the parameters it applied (it knows them because it set them, not because it read a pixel value); it is how the 'report your final parameters' requirement becomes a real, gradeable artifact bound into the proof.
inputs.realism_notes: This CSV is not pre-supplied — the agent must produce it from its own grading decisions, so the reported settings and the images they caption are forced to agree. Eight rows -> one record per page in the merge -> an eight-page merged document exported to one PDF.

outputs.name: listing_graded_web_x8
outputs.spec: Eight graded room JPEGs (sRGB, long edge 2000px), one per room, forming one matched bright-and-airy listing set. Acceptance (grader-checked, cross-image, against the in-frame grey card): on every finished frame the 18% grey card must read as a true neutral (no residual warm/cool/green/magenta tint on the card patch) and must sit at the same shared mid-grey brightness across all eight rooms (a common white/grey point). Leaning rooms (01, 03, 06) straightened to plumb verticals and cropped clean of the rotation wedge. Interiors bright-but-realistic (shadows opened, highlights held, no oversaturated fake-HDR). Glazing correctly triaged: rooms 01 and 08 have their blown windows pulled so the exterior reads through the glass; room 05's already-correct exterior is preserved while its shadowed interior is lifted. The agent neutralizes to the card by eye and reports the per-frame parameters it applied; it never reads a channel value.

outputs.name: havenkwartier_listing_proof.pdf
outputs.spec: Per-room proof: the agent-authored proof_manifest.csv (eight rows) is data-merged into havenkwartier_proof_template.indd with document_merge_data_layout, which places ONE RECORD PER PAGE to build a single merged eight-page document (eight rows -> eight pages, never more than one room per page), then document_render_layout exports that merged document to one press-ready PDF. Each page places the correct room's finished web master via the @image column (no empty frames, no image bound to the wrong room) and prints the <<room>> name plus the <<settings>> line (the agent's reported WB + exposure correction for that room) as live text. Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count = row-count = 8 is the merge gate; effective placed-image resolution >= 200 DPI at the template's image-frame size; the printed settings must match the corrections actually applied to each image.

connector_workflow.note: Upload the eight raw room frames and the authored proof .indd into the working project so the grade and the merge run against real asset references. Single plumbing call, not counted as difficulty.
Room 01 leans: straighten so the living-room wall verticals read plumb before any tonal work.
Crop away the rotation wedge left by straightening room 01 for a clean rectangular frame.

Room 01 global grade to the grey-card target: warm the cool/blue cast (temperature) and trim tint until the card LOOKS neutral by eye, set exposure so the card lands on the shared mid-grey, lift shadows, hold whites/highlights down, add gentle vibrance. Per-frame deltas chosen for THIS room's light, not a shared preset; record the temperature/tint/exposure values applied for the proof caption.
Diagnosed as a genuine blown window: select the bright left-hand garden windows to build the window-pull mask.

Masked window pull on room 01: on the window mask only, pull highlights/whites and exposure down so the blown glass recovers toward the exterior garden view. Uses image_apply_adjustments because it is the mask-accepting tonal tool; confined to the selection so the interior is untouched.

Room 02 (warm tungsten, bright, level): cool the strong orange cast (temperature down) and adjust tint until the worktop card looks neutral by eye, ease exposure/highlights DOWN slightly so its already-bright card matches the shared mid-grey, gentle vibrance. Its WB delta is opposite in sign to the cool rooms; record it for the proof.
Room 03 leans: straighten the master-bedroom verticals.
Crop the rotation wedge from straightened room 03.

Room 03 (dim + warm): the biggest exposure LIFT of the set to raise its dark card to the shared mid-grey, plus shadow lift, plus a cool WB/tint correction to neutralize the orange lamp cast on the card. A shared exposure number would leave this room too dark — its delta is unique and is recorded for the proof.

Room 04 (green fluorescent): the discriminating case — neutralize the card with a MAGENTA TINT correction (green/magenta axis), not merely a temperature shift, then set exposure to the shared mid-grey and add restrained vibrance. Getting only temperature right here leaves the card green; record the tint move.

Room 05 global grade: correct the slightly cool WB to neutralize the desk card and set overall exposure so the card hits the shared mid-grey. Do NOT globally darken — the exterior through the glass door is already correct.
Room 05 TRIAGE: select the glass garden door (the correctly-exposed bright exterior).

Invert the glass-door selection to isolate the shadowed INTERIOR foreground — the part that is actually underexposed. This is the correct opposite of a window pull; a wrong polarity here darkens the already-correct exterior.

Masked interior LIFT on room 05: raise shadows and exposure on the interior mask only so the desk/floor come up to a bright-but-realistic level, while the already-correct garden exterior (outside the mask) is preserved. The trap frame resolved correctly.
Room 06 leans: straighten the dining-room verticals.
Crop the rotation wedge from straightened room 06.

Room 06 (near-neutral): only a gentle WB nudge to sit the card exactly on the shared neutral, mild exposure to match the mid-grey, light vibrance. Deliberately restrained — over-warming this already-close card would break the common white point.

Room 07 (darkest, warm hallway): large exposure lift plus a black-point recovery (raise blacks off crushed) plus a cool WB/tint correction to bring its dark orange card to the shared neutral mid-grey. Its exposure delta is the largest lift; paired against bright room 02 to prove deltas are per-frame; record it for the proof.

Room 08 (cool, blown window) global grade: warm the cool cast and trim tint to neutralize the bed card, set exposure to the shared mid-grey, open shadows, hold highlights. Its interior deltas differ from room 01's despite both being cool blown-window frames.
Room 08 second genuine blown window: select the bright right-hand window for the window pull.

Masked window pull on room 08: pull highlights/whites and exposure down on the window mask so the neighbouring-rooftop exterior reads through the glass. Same treatment class as room 01 but its own deltas.
Downscale finished room 01 to web spec (sRGB, long edge 2000px). Downscale only, never canvas-extend.
Downscale finished room 02 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 03 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 04 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 05 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 06 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 07 to the same web spec.
Downscale finished room 08 to the same web spec; web_r1..web_r8 are the listing_graded_web_x8 deliverable and the @image targets referenced by proof_manifest.csv.

Data-merge the agent-authored proof_manifest.csv (eight rows: @image path to each web master + <<room>> name + <<settings>> = the reported per-frame WB/exposure correction the agent applied) into the authored .indd. The merge places ONE RECORD PER PAGE, emitting a single merged eight-page document (eight rows -> eight pages), each page binding the correct room image via the @image column and printing its treatment as live text. No page carries more than one record.

Export the merged eight-page document to a single press-ready PDF (one record per page). Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count = row-count = 8; each page binds the correct master at >=200 DPI at the frame; the printed <<settings>> match the corrections the agent actually applied. A collapsed or short page count means the merge failed.
Retrieve presigned URLs for the eight graded web masters and the proof PDF to surface the client hand-off package.

chaining_note: One upload (n=1) fans out into eight per-room grade sub-chains of differing depth (the depth differs because the light differs, not as padding): rooms 01/03/06 run straighten -> crop_to_bounds -> apply_adjustments; rooms 02/04/07 run a single global apply_adjustments; the glazing frames fork a mask. Room 01 (n=4->5->6) and room 08 (n=20->21->22) are diagnosed as genuine blown windows: global grade -> select_by_prompt(windows) -> masked apply_adjustments highlight/exposure pull. Room 05 (n=12->13->14->15) is diagnosed as a backlit glass door: global grade -> select_by_prompt(glass door) -> invert_selection -> masked apply_adjustments interior LIFT (the opposite polarity). Eight image_crop_and_resize calls (n=23-30) downscale each r*_final to the web spec (web_r1..web_r8). document_merge_data_layout (n=31) binds those masters + the agent-authored settings CSV into the proof template, placing one record per page to yield a merged eight-page document; document_render_layout (n=32) exports that merged document to the single press-ready proof PDF. asset_get_presigned_urls (n=33) surfaces the eight masters + the proof PDF. Every step after the upload consumes a prior named output.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon and depth-driven: 33 connector calls, 10 distinct Adobe tools, all server="adobe", but the difficulty is not step count — strip the single upload, the eight uniform web downsizes, and the delivery call and what remains is genuinely hard adaptive reasoning. The core is cross-asset colour consistency to an in-frame reference: eight rooms shot under cool daylight, warm tungsten, green fluorescent and dim tungsten must each be neutralized to the SAME grey card with per-frame WB (including a green/magenta tint case) and per-frame exposure deltas (the dim hallway needs a large lift, the bright kitchen needs a pull-down) so the whole set shares one white/grey point — the agent reasons each delta by eye and reports the parameters it applied. On top of that sits a triage: three superficially identical big-glazing frames split into two correct treatments — two masked window pulls and one inverted interior lift — where the wrong choice is invisible until the frame is inspected. It ends in an agent-owned authored endpoint: document_merge_data_layout places one record per page to build a merged eight-page document and document_render_layout exports it to a single press-ready proof PDF whose captions are the agent's own reported settings, with page-count = row-count and a DPI floor as the checkable gate. No banned capability: no HDR merge, no compositing, no generative fill/expand, no upscaling, no convert_pdf_to_indd merge target, no text-only vector merge for images, and no connector-side measurement — the agent works by eye and reports applied parameters; the grader measures the output.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a craft DECISION with a visible failure mode, never a self-measured loop): the three superficially-identical big-glazing frames must be triaged into two opposite correct treatments — rooms 01 and 08 are genuinely blown windows whose bright glass must be pulled back with a masked highlight/exposure reduction, while room 05 is a backlit glass door whose exterior is already correct and whose shadowed interior must be lifted via select-glass-door -> invert_selection -> masked interior LIFT. Choose wrong (apply the blown-window pull to room 05) and a correctly-exposed garden is darkened and the desk left in shadow — a visibly broken frame. The room-05 mask polarity (select the door, then invert to the interior) and the dependent merge (a wrong intermediate binds the wrong image or a wrong reported setting into the proof) are the other places the agent visibly trips. The agent works BY EYE and REPORTS the parameters it applied (the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure it dialed) into proof_manifest.csv; it never reads a pixel, hex, or channel value. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit rooms to one grey-card white/grey point with per-frame corrective deltas the agent must reason to by eye — a single shared preset or one WB number cannot hit it (the dim, warm, cool and green rooms each need a different, and in the green case a tint-axis, correction); (2) the glazing triage plus the constraint that only mask-accepting tonal tools may carry the window/interior edits, and the authored-.indd/@image-column discipline for the proof. THE TRAP: the naive path applies one shared white balance/exposure (or one preset) to all eight frames and treats every bright-glazing frame as a blown window; that leaves the warm/green/dim rooms visibly tinted or mis-exposed against the grey card and darkens room 05's already-correct garden exterior while leaving its desk in shadow — errors invisible until someone inspects the cards and the glass door. ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on the output, never agent-measured): every room's grey card reads neutral (no residual tint) and sits at a common mid-grey brightness across all eight; rooms 01/03/06 straightened to plumb; web masters sRGB long-edge 2000px; the proof is one merged eight-page document exported to a single PDF (page-count = row-count = 8), each page binding the correct master at >=200 DPI and printing the agent's reported per-frame WB/exposure settings, which must match the corrections actually applied.
